newsitem.title: THAILAND: Thai baht slides late, interbank rate steady.
newsitem.headline: Thai baht slides late, interbank rate steady.

text.p: The baht continued to slide against the dollar late on Wednesday as the U.S. unit surged against major currencies in overseas markets, dealers said.
The baht tumbled to 25.798-25.808 to the dollar in late trade from 25.739-25.744 in early morning and 25.725-25.730 late on Tuesday, dealers said.
"The dollar is very bullish abroad. Heavy buying of the dollar emerged when the U.S. unit broke 119 yen," said one dealer at a foreign bank.
They said the baht fall was solely due to the American unit's strength and not due to any speculative attack on it.
The Bank of Thailand on Wednesday fixed the baht/dollar mid-rate at 25.75, the lowest since August 21, 1991. The mid-rate was at 25.74 on Tuesday.
The one-month baht/dollar swap premium was steady 8.00/9.00 per a dollar late against 8.50/9.50 in the morning.
Dealers said the higher liquidity and lower short-term baht interest rates also diverted some demand for the dollar.

The overnight interbank rate eased further late on Wednesday as banks tried to lend out surplus cash after the passing of the central bank's reserve requirement today, dealers said. Banks must meet the requirements on seventh and 22nd of every month. "Most banks appeared to maintain too much funds for the reserve requirement. So they tried to offload them today," said another dealer.
The overnight interbank rate eased to 8.00-8.50 percent late from 8.50 in the morning trade, dealers said.
